newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt supply to continue at brisk pace.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt supply to continue at brisk pace.

text.p: The onslaught of supply pouring into the corporate bond primary market is expected to continue as U.S. Treasury yields remain at their lowest levels since early spring, dealers said.
"There are still plenty of names out there...we should see several issues come to market today," said one high-grade syndicate source.
On Wednesday, Transamerica Corp priced $200 million in A2/A rated 10-year notes to yield 60 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. Morgan Stanley & Co was lead underwriter on the deal.

Among other issues expected to price on Wednesday are CoreStates Financial Corp $200 million 10-year debt offering via JP Morgan Securities. Price talk on the issue is seen at 60 to 62 basis points over Treasuries, syndicate sources said.

Also, Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc is expected to price a two-part debt offering via CS First Boston, syndicate sources said. The first tranche is expected to consist of $200 million in 10-year debt with price talk seen at 130 to 135 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
The second tranche is seen at $200 million in 30-year debt with price talk in the 110 basis points arena, sources added.
On Tuesday, about $1.5 billion in new straight corporate debt was priced in the corporate bond primary market, dealers said.
A recent drop in U.S. Treasury yields has spurred a flood of new issues as U.S. corporations, lured by lower interest rates, capitalize on the favorable environment to finance debt.
Wachovia Corp, Bristol-Myers Squibb Co, Travelers/Aetna Property Casualty Corp, ITT Corp and Commercial Credit were among Tuesday's investment grade issuers.
In the private placement market, Dollar Financial issued $110 million in 144A notes in Tuesday's business as well.
"Yesterday's deals were well received," said one high-grade syndicate source said. "The market (Treasury) performing very well helped most of the them."
Still, syndicate sources said, another $1.0 billion in private placement debt offerings are expected to hit the market this week.
Celestica International is expected to issue $150 million in 144A senior subordianted guaranteed notes.
Blue Bird Body is expected to price $100 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006 via Merrill Lynch. Price talk on the isuse is seen at 10.75 to 11.0 percent, dealers said.
Another $100 million is expected to come to market from Atrium Cos, dealers added.
Cole National Corp is also expected to price $140 million in 144A notes due 2006 via CIBC Wood Gundy.
In addition, IMED Corp may price $175 million 144A senior subordinated notes due 2006 via Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is off 4/32 at 100-20/32 to yield 6.45 percent.
